title: Kailasagiri Cave Temple & Kaiwara
tagline: Bangalore → Hoskote → H Cross → Kaiwara (Bheema-Bakasura Betta, 500 steps) → Kailasagiri hand-cut cave temple → Chintamani → Devanahalli → Bangalore. ~180 km, a half-day loop east of the city.
summary: The easy one in the collection: a Sunday loop east of Bangalore built around Kailasagiri, a hill outside Chintamani where a cave has been cut by hand into the rock and lined with shrines — Vallabha Ganapati, Chaturmukhalingeshwara and Jagadambe — reached by a short stone-paved walk you do barefoot. Pair it with Kaiwara, 7 km away, where the Bheema-Bakasura Betta climb (about 500 steps) earns a view over the Kolar plains. Go out on the Hoskote–H Cross road and come back through Devanahalli so you never repeat tarmac.

credit.note: '50 km from Bengaluru — a cave temple, a hilltop view'; it's nearer 75 km, but the point stands

segments.note: The only dull bit; get it done before the traffic wakes up.

segments.road: Hoskote – Sidlaghatta road to H Cross
segments.note: Two-lane state road through mulberry and grape country; watch for tractors and silk-cocoon lorries.
Quiet rural road. Kaiwara is the Yogi Narayana ashram town; the Bheema-Bakasura Betta steps start behind it.
Short hop through the hills. Park at the base; the cave is a 10-minute walk up a stone path, barefoot.
Lunch stop. Chintamani has proper fuel and food.
The return leg on a different road: open plateau, windmills on the ridges, very little traffic.

highlights: Kailasagiri's hand-cut cave — a low, cool tunnel through the rock with shrines set into the walls, unlike any other temple this close to the city.
Bheema-Bakasura Betta at Kaiwara — 500 steps to a rock summit with the Kolar plains laid out below; do it first, before the sun is up properly.
The Chintamani–Devanahalli plateau road — empty, straight, and lined with wind turbines.

offroad.summary: Tarmac end to end. This is a road-bike loop; the only 'trail' is the stone path at Kailasagiri and the steps at Kaiwara.
notes: The stone path at Kailasagiri gets hot by midday — footwear comes off at the base, so carry socks or go early.
Rural roads have unmarked speed breakers at every village; hold 60 and look ahead.
Kaiwara's steps are steep and uneven; not one for riding boots.

timings: Kailasagiri cave temple is open through the day; go before 10 AM for cool stone and empty paths.
No permits or fees beyond small parking charges.
Fuel: Hoskote, Chintamani, Devanahalli — no gaps to worry about.
cautions: Weekend crowds at Kaiwara ashram around festivals; the hill itself stays quiet.
The Hoskote stretch of NH 75 has heavy truck traffic — the earlier the better.
